title: HTTP Interceptors
summary: Run code on every request and response — auth tokens, errors, logging.
heading: HTTP Interceptors

blocks.text: An interceptor is a function that sits between your app and the server. Every HTTP request passes through it on the way out, and every response on the way back — so it's the perfect place to do something for all calls at once: attach an auth token, log requests, show a loading bar, or handle errors globally.
Instead of adding the same header or try/catch in every service method, you write it once in an interceptor.
A modern interceptor is a function of type HttpInterceptorFn. It receives the request and a next function to pass it along. Register interceptors with withInterceptors.

blocks.text: You can inject() services inside an interceptor, just like in a guard.
Use the RxJS catchError operator on the response stream to deal with failures in one place — for example, logging out and redirecting on a 401 Unauthorized.

blocks.text: Interceptors run in the order you list them: withInterceptors([authInterceptor, errorInterceptor]).
